task.title: Add comments and lightweight attachments, markdown formatting
task.description:
Add comments, lightweight attachments (files and links), and markdown rendering to tasks. (Design agreed 2026-08-13. Depends on WB-01KZYH9C0JRQX0N46JHZ929XC4 — the new operation types below must ship carrying the writer-format marker.)

## Design

**Comments.** Three new task operation types: comment.add {id, body}, comment.edit {commentId, body}, comment.remove {commentId} — comment IDs minted like operation IDs, attribution and timestamps from the op envelope. The checkpoint state.json materializes the live thread (body, author, created/edited times, edited flag), ordered by creation. Edit/remove of a nonexistent comment refuses at the mutation boundary; replay converges tolerantly per the standing collection semantics — concurrent edits converge deterministically by op order, full history in show --history, no new conflict type.

**Attachments.** One unified list, two kinds: file and link. attachment.add {id, name, kind, media, size, ...} / attachment.remove {id}. File blobs live in the adding commit's tree beside operation.json; the checkpoint lists live attachments by blob OID (reads are one cat-file, under the 4 MiB plumbing ceiling). Caps enforced at the mutation boundary: 1 MiB per file, 10 MiB live total per task, refusals suggesting a link instead. Links are URL + label, http(s) only, zero storage. HARD REQUIREMENT (compaction reachability invariant): a blob is reachable only through its own task's ref history — no shared store, no cross-task dedup — so the future compaction verb (WB-01KYD75B1R6CW2ZGCC0YEQ7Q28) gets keep/strip-attachments modes for free. Removal hides an attachment but reclaims nothing until compaction; the docs say so.

**CLI — comments and attachments are nouns on a task, so they ride the existing verbs, not new ones:**
- workbook update <id> --comment <body>  (add)
- workbook update <id> --edit-comment <comment-id> --comment <body>  (the body travels in --comment, since a flag carries one value)
- workbook update <id> --remove-comment <comment-id>
- workbook update <id> --attach-file <path>  /  --attach-url <url> [--attach-label <text>]
- workbook update <id> --remove-attachment <id>
- workbook show <id> --get-attachment <id> [--out <path>]
Combining these with other update flags emits one atomic pack (update X --status done --comment "shipped" is one history entry). workbook show renders the thread and the attachment list.

**Web.** Task page grows a comments thread and an attachments section (upload, list, download, remove) via /api/tasks/{id}/comments[/{cid}] and /api/tasks/{id}/attachments[/{aid}], expectedHead as everywhere. Security rule (load-bearing): the attachment GET serves ONLY image/* inline; everything else downloads with Content-Disposition: attachment + nosniff — serving attached HTML inline would be stored XSS on the board's origin.

**Markdown.** Client-side subset renderer (SSR rejected 2026-08-13: it would break optimistic paint or force two parity-locked renderers, and would open the client's first trusted-HTML path): headings, bold/italic, inline + fenced code, lists, blockquotes, links — building DOM nodes directly, NEVER innerHTML; unsupported syntax falls back to plain text. Applied to descriptions (task page gains read mode <-> edit mode; board cards render formatting under their existing clamp) and comment bodies. Images ONLY as attachment references (![alt](attachment:<id>) -> the GET endpoint) — no external image URLs (tracking beacon on every board view). CLI show keeps printing raw markdown.

**Delivery.** Four PRs: PR-1 core ops + caps + replay/conflict tests (carrying the writer-format marker); PR-2 CLI on update/show; PR-3 web endpoints + task-page UI; PR-4 markdown renderer across board/task/comments. UI PRs carry measured viewport usability checks in both implementation and review briefs.

## Shipped (2026-08-15)

Four PRs, each through adversarial execution-verified review (records on the PRs):

- **PR #99 (core, three review rounds).** Five operation types at generation 1 (the marker machinery's first real consumer), checkpoint thread + unified attachment list, blob-in-commit-tree storage with growth-enforced ceilings (1 MiB / 10 MiB / counts), the compaction reachability invariant pinned, link validation, one-pack composition via UpdateInput intents. The review found and forced the fix of a release-critical hole beyond the story's scope: tree shape was judged BEFORE the marker, so any future release adding a tree entry would have read as corrupt-data forever — tree-entry recognition now runs post-decode behind the marker gate on both the task and config sides, with the structural floor (documents present, regular blobs — a round-3 mode regression caught and fixed) enforced at every generation. Also: SVG refused as a stored image media type at both layers; a class of passes-for-the-wrong-reason tests (topology masking) rooted out of the whole forgery suite.
- **PR #100 (CLI, two rounds).** The update flag family (--comment, --edit-comment, --remove-comment, --attach-file, --attach-url/--attach-label, --remove-attachment), show thread/attachment rendering, show --get-attachment [--out]. Whole-ID display with prefix acceptance (same-pack ULIDs share their 10-char timestamp). Review caught a real bug — --attach-file on a character device read unbounded (14 GB in 4s) and a FIFO hung forever; fixed with an IsRegular gate whose revert hangs the test at the exact frame — plus the resolve-after-fetch guarantee getting its two-clone witness, and the usage-agreement test's exceptions tightened. Blob reads moved behind Service.AttachmentContent.
- **PR #102 (web, two rounds + a reviewer provenance correction).** Task-page comments thread and attachments UI; JSON+base64 upload (multipart is CORS-simple and GuardSameOrigin exists for a reason) with a per-route body ceiling; the attachment GET serving a four-type raster allow-list inline and everything else as a download under nosniff + a per-response default-src 'none'; sandbox CSP. The stored-XSS surface held under a full real-browser assault. Review fixed the tautological CSP pin, the untested BlobReads wiring, a silent invalid-URL swallow, a file+Enter misroute, and hit-target widths.
- **PR #103 (markdown, two rounds).** Hand-rolled DOM-building subset renderer (16 elements, 5 attributes, whitelist-walked on all three surfaces), headings capped below the page's own, links through safeLinkURL, images only as attachment references degrading by type through the allow-listed route with the inline set published once as data-inline-media. Review blocker: the page CSP had no img-src, so every rendered image was browser-blocked — invisible to the fake-DOM harness by construction (the lesson is recorded: new resource types need real-browser load proof). Also fixed: a bracket-pairing phishing primitive (labels forged across earlier brackets), the whitelist walk's style blindness, and honest prose for backslashes and the time bound. Two measurement-driven card layout fixes shipped with order-pinned CSS.

**Noted residuals (accepted):** --compare does not diff a thread (history describes every op); comment/attachment echo lines are unbounded like descriptions; U+202E display survival filed as WB-01KZZ6GXEGCAJBBQG0W1ZEZT04; the duplicate-ULID projection wedge (pre-existing) filed as WB-01KZYY9RYKNMETM7XBT4NEV4MD; adjacent literal text beside an honest link is inherent to any renderer.
